deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to an axiomatic development of 'modéré' (tame) geometry. Grothendieck works over a base R, presumably a real closed field or ℝ. Some subsets of the R^n are declared 'modérées' (tame), subject to axioms (M1), (M2), …. 'Espaces modérés' are built from these, forming a category Esp_M with an underlying-set functor X ↦ |X|. In section (V), 'Relations avec topologies', R is assumed topological and Hausdorff, and axiom (M9) is imposed: tame subsets of R^n are compact.

The argument on this page runs as follows.
(1) Because tame parts are compact, |·| factors through compact topological spaces. A tame map has a tame, hence compact, graph. Projecting the compact graph onto the source gives a continuous bijection from a compact space onto a Hausdorff space, which is a homeomorphism; so the map is continuous. The resulting functor Esp_M → (compact spaces) is claimed to be faithful, conservative, 'transportable' and (in an added note) left exact. Faithfulness holds because the underlying set already determines the map. Conservativity holds because the inverse of a tame bijection has the transposed graph, which is again tame.
(2) An example follows, only partly legible. It seems to involve a closed set in M_1 (tame subsets of R) and a (simplicial?) complex Σ such that every simplex of Σ embeds in some R^n. That is, polyhedra or finite simplicial complexes are given as basic tame spaces.
(3) Every tame space (not necessarily compact) receives the 'locally tame' topology: the final, weak topology with respect to its tame parts, analogous to CW or compactly generated topologies. Under a separation hypothesis ('modérément séparé', glossed as something like 'loci of convergent sequences of tame spaces'), this topology induces on each tame part its own compact topology.
(4) One would like every point of a tame space to have a fundamental system of tame neighbourhoods, apparently contractible ones (the insertion is hard to read). Grothendieck says it suffices to require this in R, hence in the R^n, and records it as axiom (M10): every point of R has a fundamental system of neighbourhoods belonging to M_1.
The next page goes on to localise tameness of maps, giving a sheaf of tame maps and the sheaf of germs of tame functions.

Mathematically this is an axiomatic precursor of o-minimal / tame topology. Here tame sets are compact, closer to semialgebraic or subanalytic compact sets and polyhedra. Non-compact spaces are glued from them with the weak topology.
errors: 'Il suffit que ce soit vrai dans R, donc dans les R^n' is a gap if the neighbourhoods are meant to be contractible. Small tame neighbourhoods in R^n of points of an arbitrary tame subset need not follow from the property in R alone. One needs something like local conic structure or a triangulation theorem, as in o-minimal geometry.

Possible tension: R (or R^n) is not compact, so with (M9) R itself cannot be a tame part. (M10) then makes R locally compact via compact tame neighbourhoods, and global objects must be 'espaces modérés' with the weak topology. The text does not spell this out.

'Left exact' for the functor to compact spaces needs fibre products of tame spaces to be computed by set-theoretic fibre products with the subspace topology. This is plausible given (M9) and Hausdorffness, but unproved here.

ideas.what: Axiom that tame subsets are compact; forgetful functor from tame spaces to compact Hausdorff spaces, faithful, conservative, left exact; continuity of tame maps via compactness of graphs
ideas.modern_name: Topology of definable / semialgebraic compact sets; closed-graph argument

ideas.where_published: Only the programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5 (1984); not this axiomatics

ideas.what: Tame spaces glued from compact tame parts carrying the weak ('localement modérée') topology
ideas.modern_name: Locally semialgebraic / weakly semialgebraic spaces; definable spaces with weak topology

ideas.what: Axiom (M10): every point of R has a fundamental system of tame neighbourhoods; desire for contractible tame neighbourhood systems
ideas.modern_name: Local conic structure / local contractibility of definable sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimal geometry (van den Dries, Tame Topology and o-minimal Structures, 1998; Coste)

missed.claim: A numbered axiom system (M1)–(M10) for tame geometry, developed in Grothendieck's notes around 1973–78. It includes a compactness axiom (M9) and a neighbourhood axiom (M10), and frames tame spaces categorically: a faithful, conservative, left exact functor to compact spaces, plus sheaves of tame maps. This predates the o-minimality literature. It is a historical datum not generally recorded; Esquisse only alludes to such a programme.
missed.quote: (M9) Les parties modérées de R^n sont compactes … (M10) Dans R, tt pt a un syst. fond. de voisinages ∈ M_1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents an independent, categorically oriented axiomatisation of tame topology, one based on compact tame parts and a 'transportable' forgetful functor. This is relevant to the history of o-minimality and to current categorical treatments of tame or definable spaces.

deep.surprise_reason: Historically interesting evidence of an early, pre-o-minimal axiomatic tame topology with a categorical flavour. The mathematics on this page itself is routine and the specific statements are known in semialgebraic and o-minimal geometry.
